thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired (P1) for service=model-serving-us-east (region: us-east-2, zone: az-east-2) — high 5xx rate and increased tail latency. https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD12345

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Triggered on: model-serving-us-east - Error rate > 5% for 2m. Priority: P1. Summary link: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/1769748888

sam: seeing a spike in 502/503 and some connection resets from our inference shards. Affects both hosted and dedicated pools in us-east-2.

priya: confirmed in grafana — error rate jumped ~7% at 14:54 UTC, median latency up from 120ms -> 320ms, p95 to 2.1s. KV cache evictions also spiking.

mike: paging oncall now. sam, can you check shard-controller logs? I saw a few OOM-kill events on node-37 earlier.

sam: tailing shard-controller: 
```
2026-03-15T14:53:22Z shard-ctrl[shard-17]: reconnect failed: context deadline exceeded
2026-03-15T14:53:24Z shard-ctrl[shard-17]: evicting prefix cache (total=124MB -> reclaim)
2026-03-15T14:54:01Z kernel: OutOfMemory: killed process redwood-infer (pid 4123)
```

olga: incident-bot shows automated failover didn't trigger. Looks like region fallback policy had a cooldown due to previous flaps.

diane: PagerDuty: sam acknowledged the alert at 14:55 UTC. Escalating to senior SRE per runbook.

sam: ack - I'm on it. Quick status: noisy OOMs in az-east-2b nodes running model-x-large-quant; cold-starts failing causing 502s.

priya: customer impact: some streaming responses truncated; avg token throughput dropped for hosted customers pinned to model-x-large-quant. Not seeing embedding errors yet.

eng-oncall: plan per runbook: 1) divert new traffic away from az-east-2b -> us-east-1a for hosted API, 2) coordinate Dedicated pool burst to fallback smaller quantized variant (model-x-large-q4_0) for degraded but stable service, 3) drain and recycle affected nodes, 4) enable prefix-cache warming.

sam: starting traffic divert now. Command: 
```
# divert 25% traffic off az-east-2b to us-east-1a for model-serving-us-east
redwoodctl route update --service model-serving-us-east --from az-east-2b --to us-east-1a --percent 25
```

mike: executing fallback rollout for dedicated pools:
```
redwoodctl rollout create --service dedicated-models --variant model-x-large-q4_0 --strategy canary --percent 10
```

olga: adding runbook note: cooldown prevented autopager. We should revisit policy. filing follow-up ticket after mitigation.

sam: node drain in progress for node-37 and node-42. Using graceful drain with 30s token flush: 
```
ssh node-37
systemctl stop redwood-infer
redwoodctl node drain node-37 --grace 30
```

priya: notifying customer-ops: some enterprise customers in us-east-2 may see transient 5xx or longer responses. No full outage, partial degradation. ETA on mitigation?

eng-oncall: expected stabilization in 10-15m after divert+canary. Will update after second checkpoint.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: Escalation sent to oncall-sre-secondary at 14:58 UTC (no ack yet).

sam: can we increase cache size on the fallback variant? It helps reduce cold-start token cost.

mike: yes, bumping prefix-cache to 200MB for the canary variant: 
```
redwoodctl config set variant/model-x-large-q4_0 cache.prefix_size=200MB
```

olga: quick note: we saw NIC errors on node-42 before OOMs. Might be hardware requeue causing backlog then oom. Opening hardware ticket with cloud provider.

diane: PagerDuty: oncall-sre-secondary acked at 14:59 UTC. Assigned to olga.

priya: running synthetic checks against hosted endpoints — initial 25% divert reduced 5xx by ~60% for affected customers. p95 still elevated but trending down.

sam: recycle complete for node-37, node-42. Kernel OOM root cause likely job mis-scheduler; we've added a hard memory cap for model-x-large on these nodes in cloud agent.

mike: increasing canary traffic to 40% and promoting fallback to 60%. Command: 
```
redwoodctl rollout promote --id canary-7890 --percent 60
```

eng-oncall: coordinate with support: please post templated customer message. Priya, can you take point?

priya: drafting: "We're experiencing degraded responses in us-east-2. We've rerouted traffic and enabled a fallback model to restore availability. You may see higher latency or truncated streams for a short period. We'll follow up once fully stabilized." Will post to status page and notify affected accounts via email.

incident-bot: Logged incident: INC-20260315-1769748888. Severity=P1. Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/INC-20260315-1769748888

olga: provider ticket opened: CLOUD-98765. They acknowledge packet drops in az-east-2b between 14:48-14:56 UTC.

sam: final checks: no new OOMs in last 3m, 5xx rate down to 0.8%, p95 down to 420ms. Continuing to monitor.

diane: great job. We'll keep traffic diverted for 30m, then gradual failback after proving stability. Postmortem owners: olga (infra), sam (runtime), mike (rollout), priya (customer comms).

eng-oncall: closing PD incident once metrics stable for 15m. Next update in 10m.

priya: posted incident note to status.redwood.ai and emailed top 10 enterprise customers.

sam: follow-up action items created: revisit autopager cooldowns, add NIC health checks to early-warning, add automatic model-variant fallback when OOM signature detected.

mike: adding replication test for prefix-cache warming in staging.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: Incident resolved (auto-close) at 15:08 UTC. Resolution: traffic diverted and fallback variant promoted; hardware packet drops confirmed and provider remediation scheduled.

priya: marking thread resolved here. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:"
